One-shot constrained triangulation

Source: R/lari.R
lari_triangulate.Rd

Build a mesh, optionally refine it, and return the tables: the same shape as cdtr's one-shot call, for use as a drop-in backend.

lari_triangulate(
  x,
  y,
  s0 = NULL,
  s1 = NULL,
  PA = NULL,
  max_area = NULL,
  min_angle = NULL,
  min_edge_length = NULL,
  erase = c("outer", "holes", "hull"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x, y

vertex coordinates (may be omitted for an empty mesh)

s0, s1

1-based indices into x/y of constraint segment start and end (may be NULL)

PA

optional numeric matrix (or data frame) of per-vertex attributes, one row per vertex, e.g. cbind(z_ = z). New vertices (crossings, Steiner points) get linearly interpolated values. The attribute columns are fixed when the mesh is created.

max_area

maximum triangle area, NULL for none

min_angle

minimum triangle angle in degrees, NULL for none. Above about 20.7 degrees termination is not guaranteed by theory; the floor keeps it finite.

min_edge_length

the edge-length floor; NULL chooses default_min_edge_length() from the current segments and the area bound, taking the smaller of max_area and the finest area the sizing field asks for so a sizing field is honoured rather than capped; 0 never gives up

erase

which region is meshed: "outer" (everything inside the outermost constraints, depth > 0), "holes" (odd depth only), or "hull"

...

passed to lari_refine() (size, max_steiner, seeds)

Value

a list with vertices, triangles, segments, unrefined (NULL when no refinement was asked for) and min_edge_length

Examples

r <- lari_triangulate(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1), 1:4, c(2, 3, 4, 1), max_area = 0.05)
str(r)
#> List of 6
